First, we let

$$
L={lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{{x}^{2}-25}{x-5}.
$$

Comparing this with the formula for the instantaneous rate of change

$$
{f}^{′}(a)={lim}_{x\to a}\frac{f(x)-f(a)}{x-a},
$$

we see that if we let $f(x)={x}^{2}$ and $a=5$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}^{′}(5) & ={lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{f(x)-f(5)}{x-5} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{{x}^{2}-{5}^{2}}{x-5} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to 5}\frac{{x}^{2}-25}{x-5}=L.\end{aligned}
$$

This confirms that $L={f}^{′}(5).$

Computing the derivative, we have

$$
{f}^{′}(x)=2x,\,{f}^{′}(5)=2\cdot 5=10,
$$

and therefore, we conclude that $L=10.$
